trickyParts: The browser's reader counts a blank line toward a list item's spread where no list or quote the item holds is open across it and the line is not one of the endings the item drops. A typed block is no such container, so a blank line anywhere inside one is the item's - but three things keep it: a line the containers around the block do not read as blank, a block inside it that takes it (an unclosed fenced code block, a list or quote open across it, and, in a quote, a list the line follows), and the item's own ending, which costs a second blank line where no fence closes the block, except at the end of a quote-less document and before the list's next item.

The writer's own output had to move with the reader: with the item read spread, a tight item's typed block written with a blank line between two blocks read back spread, which the write path refuses. Writing those blocks with the item's tight lines fixes it and makes one document readback_test.go pinned storable, which is why that test loses an entry.

A typed block a footnote definition in the item holds is refused rather than read. Three attempts to read it as the browser does each moved more of the family wrong than they fixed (264 misread, then 294, then 432, then 444), because that parser's reading of the definition's own end and of the item's blank lines meet there. The merged base refuses every document this refuses, so the gate holds.
